p_question-5650.ja:
以下は、留学生の作文である。

「落語」体験

バラージベーテル

　今回、留学生センターで行われた文化体験のテーマは「落語」だった。落語は日本の伝統的な芸能の一つだ。着物を着た落語家が舞台に正座したまま、一人で何役も演じ、話って聞かせる。たいていは、面白く、おかしい話だ。私の国には演劇はあるが、落語のようなものはない。

　私は、文化体験が落語だと知って、実はがっかりした。以前、ある落語を授業で読んだが、あまり面白いと[48]話をただ聞いているのは退屈だろうと思ったし、聞き取れるかどうかも不安だった。

[49]落語を聞いている間、私はよく笑った。落語家の動作や声の出し方は本当に面白くて、場面の様子もよくわかった。しぐさや話し方を変えて、親と子供など二役以上を一人で演じ、会話を進める。座ったまま体を揺らして歩いている様子を見せ、家から店に移動したことを表す。食事の動作は、本当に何かを食べているようだった。

　文化体験が終わったとき、落語の印象がすっかり変わっていた。落語とは、落語家の動作と語りを同時に[50]。私は、話の細部は理解できていなかったかもしれない。しかし、落語家の動作と語りを通して、登場人物の性格や暮らしが感じられた。それに、映像や音楽や踊りがなくても、生き生きと話を伝え、人を笑わせられる落語家の表現力にも感動した。

　落語には、怖い話や感動的な話もあるそうだ。落語家は[51]をするのだろうか。ぜひいろいろな落語を聞いてみたい。

The following is an essay by an international student.

Experiencing “Rakugo”

バラージベーテル

　This time, the theme of the cultural activity held at the International Student Center was “rakugo.” Rakugo is one of Japan’s traditional performing arts. A rakugo storyteller, dressed in kimono, remains seated in seiza on the stage and alone plays several roles, telling stories to the audience. Most of the stories are amusing and funny. In my country we have theater, but nothing like rakugo.

　When I found out that the cultural activity was rakugo, to be honest, I was disappointed. Previously, we had read a rakugo story in class, but it wasn’t very interesting, so [48] I thought that just listening to a story would probably be boring, and I was also worried about whether I would be able to understand it.

[49] While I was listening to the rakugo, I laughed a lot. The performer’s movements and the way he used his voice were truly entertaining, and I could clearly picture the scenes. By changing his gestures and way of speaking, he alone played two or more roles—such as a parent and child—and carried the dialogue forward. While remaining seated, he rocked his body to show walking, indicating that the scene had moved from a house to a shop. His eating motions really looked as if he were eating something.

　By the time the activity ended, my impression of rakugo had completely changed. Rakugo is something that [50] the storyteller’s actions and narration at the same time. I may not have understood all the details of the story. However, through the performer’s actions and narration, I could sense the characters’ personalities and their lives. Moreover, even without video, music, or dance, I was impressed by the rakugo performer’s expressive power to convey a story vividly and make people laugh.

　I hear that rakugo also includes scary stories and moving stories. I wonder if rakugo performers also [51]. I definitely want to listen to various rakugo stories.

最近は、環境のためによい商品が市場に多く出ているが、それらを求める際にとても便利なインターネットのサイトが、ある環境団体によって運営されている。そのサイトには、環境のことを考えた家電製品からホテルまで10分類、1万点もの商品・サービスの情報がある。

p_question-5658.ja:
（５）

人材の評価や選抜の方式は、社会の根本的な活力を規定する最も重要な（注1）ファクターである。しかもその人材の育成には時間がかかる。競争のない社会、公正な評価が通らない組織は、長い目で見れば必ず（注2）衰退する。だからこそ、いつの時代でも、どの組織でも、優秀な人材の獲得に（注3）躍起になり、人材の育成に多大の努力を注ぐとともに、いかに公正な評価のシステムを組み込むのかという点に強い関心を払ってきたのである。

（注1）ファクター：要素

（注3）躍起になる：必死になる

p_question-5659.ja:
（１）

次の文章は、ある小学校の先生が自分のクラスについて書いたものである。

　５年生を受け持った時の５月、T男が（注１）つぶやいた。「僕はやりたくないなあ。だって、どうせ僕にはいいところなんてないもん」。クラスの友達の「いいところ探し」をしようと提案した時のことだ。　クラス替えをしたばかりで、まだ子ども同士の関係が深まっていない時期である。友達のことを知ってほしい、長所を見つける目を持ってほしい、という意図で提案した。T男のつぶやきを聞き、自信をつけさせるチャンスになるかもしれない、と考えた。「その人のいいところや、良さを見つけた場面などを書きましょう」と全員の名前を書いたプリントを配布した。プリントを前に、ニコニコしながら書く子、友達の顔をちらちらと見て書く子、難しい顔で考え込む子など様々だ。それでも表情を見ているだけで、子どもたちが一生懸命友達の良さを見つけようとしている様子が伝わってきた。

　T男を見ると、全く書けていない。小声で伝えた。「T男くんの良いところを書いてくれている人がたくさんいるよ」「うそだー」「うそじゃないよ。習字がうまいとか、係の仕事をちゃんとやっているとか」。聞いて（注２）まんざらでもないといった表情である。続きを翌週までに仕上げておくことにした。T男も全員分の長所の記入ができた。　提出されたものをまとめ、冊子にして配布した。自分の長所について書かれたものを読んでいる子どもたちは、T男を含め誰もが、照れくさいけれどうれしい、といった表情だった。（注１）つぶやく：小さな声でひとりごとを言う（注２）まんざらでもない：必ずしも嫌ではない

p_question-5662.ja:
（２）

　作り声は「本当の自分の姿を出したくない」という思いの表れでもあります。（中略）　日本には、話す人が違ってもまるで同じ人であるかのような「職業声」があります。その仕事に就く人は「自分はこんな声にならないといけない」と思い込んでいるかのようです。　特に（注１）接客業や営業職に多く見られる職業声は、まるで声なマニュアルや制服と同じように扱っているように感じます。自分の本来の声を職業声で覆ってしまうことで、「仕事を言われたとおりにやっていますよ」「自分はこの仕事をする人になりきっていますよ」と暗に示しているのです。自分の個性を消して（注２）うわべの職業声で話すことは、厳しい見方をすれば、人間対人間の場面で、個人を放棄しているとも言えますわ。個人の（注３）放棄は責任の放棄ともたやすく繋がります。

　制服を着てしまうと組織の一員となって個人は消える。職業声も同じです。仕事に個性などいらないということでしょうか。しかし一日の三分の一は仕事をしているわけですから、その時間を制服のような借り物の声で話すことは、気楽ではあるかもしれないけれど、心身には大きな負担であろうと思います。
（注１）接客業：飲食店やホテルなどで客に接する職業（注２）うわべの：表面的な（注３）放棄する：捨てる

p_question-5664.ja:
(3) 
　数年前、家を引っ越した。50年住み慣れた小さな家だったが、いざ引っ越しとなると、使っていない道具がごろごろ出てきて、あらためてものの多さにびっくりした。

　道具にしろ、本にしろずいぶん多量に所有していて、これを（注1）使いこなし、（注2）読みつくすには多量の時間がかかる。あと何年生きられるだろうと人生を逆算してみて、①この物最はムダだなぁと引っ越しのトラックの助手席で考えた。

　私は世間の人よりはものの所有欲が強いとは思っていない。むしろものをもたないほうと思っているが、それでもものが多過ぎるのである。

　昔、「預かりものの思想」と言った人がいる。人はぽつんと生まれて、ぷつんと消えていく。家や土地、道具にしても、いくら自分の所有だとカンでみても、死んでしまえばもっていけない。いずれは世の中に返していかなければならない。このわずかな人生の時間の中で、②それを楽しむしかないのだ。空気や水と同じように、土地も家も道具も、あらゆる諸物は世の中から預かって、生きている間だけ借りているのだ、という考えだった。たしかに、私たちはものへの所有欲が強い。車をもつ、家をもつ、高級ブランド品をもつ、携帯電話をもつ、コンピューターをもつ、所有することで満足感を得ている。しかし、所有欲をふくらませるには、どこかで限界があるだろう。

　「預かりものの思想」は、そういう（注3）物欲にかられる私たちに冷水をかける思想だった。

（注1）使いこなす：ここでは、すべて使う 
（注2）読みつくす：すべて読む 
（注3）物欲にかられる：物欲を抑えられなくなる

p_question-5669.ja:
（注１）ネットワークにつながったコンピュータには「オフライン状態」と「オンライン状態」があります。オフライン状態のコンピュータは、外部と（注２）交信せずに、すでにインプットされている情報やソフトウェアを用いて作業しています。一方、オンライン状態のコンピュータは、インターネットなどで外部と交信しながら新しい情報やソフトウェアを取り入れながら作業します。人間にもまた、オフライン状態とオンライン状態があるようです。オフライン状態はいわば日常生活で、あまり新しいことを取り入れることはありませんが、オンライン状態では新しい情報を取り入れて、自分の行動や思考を変えていきます。

　ぼくの場合、旅行に出ると自然にオンライン状態になります。いま住んでいる日本にいても当然、オンライン状態になることがありますが、旅に出れば、どちらを向いても新しい情報がたくさんあるので自然にオンラインになるのです。

　動物は皆、（注３）本能にもとづいて習慣的に行動します。人間もまた動物で、強い習慣性があります。そして、習慣的なことに対しては、毎日の生活で疑問に感じることなどありません。しかし旅に出ると、非日常的な環境に放り出されます。そうすると、自分がいままであたりまえにやっていたことに疑問を抱くきっかけが生まれます。日々、あたりまえのようにやっていたことにも別なやり方があることに気づくのです。それがオフラインからオンラインになることにつながります。旅先でなら、自分とは違うことをしている人を見て、単に「こいつらは変だ」とか「おかしい」と思うのではなく、「この国の人は皆こういうようにやっているようだから、（注４）一理あるんじゃないか」と考えることができ、（注５）ひいては「自分でもやってみようじゃないか」となります。そして、こういった経験を通して自分のそれまでのやり方、人生を考え直すことになるのです。（中略）

「灯台下暗し」という諺があります。「広辞苑」によると「灯台（燈台）の直下はあかりが暗いように、（注６）手近の事情はかえってわかりにくいものである」とあります。ふだんの環境にあって自分の人生を考え直したり、（注７）おさらいしたりしようと思っても、それは難しいのです。だから、ちょっと離れて自分のことを考えるために旅に出るのです。

（注１）ネットワーク：ここでは、インターネットなど（注２）交信する：通信し合う（注３）本能：生まれつき持っている性質（注４）理ある：もっともな理由がある（注５）ひいては：さらに（注６）手近の：身近な（注７）おさらいする：ここでは、振り返る

questions.stem: 美しい情景が目に浮かんだ。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: じょうけい is correct.

**Question Translation**  
"美しい情景が目に浮かんだ。"  
→ "A beautiful scene came to mind."

**Explanation**  
The kanji "情景" is read as **じょうけい**, which means *scene* or *sight*. This reading fits the context of the sentence, describing a mental image of a beautiful scene.

**Other Options**  
2. じょけい – Not a standard reading of 情景.  
3. じょうえい – Means *projection* or *screening* (kanji: 上映), incorrect for 情景.  
4. じょえい – Not a standard reading or meaning related to 情景.

Only **じょうけい** correctly matches the kanji **情景** in this context.
questions.expl_ko:
정답: 1번 「情景(じょうけい)」 — 정경, 광경. 「目に浮かぶ」와 잘 어울린다.
오답: 2 じょけい·3 じょうえい·4 じょえい는 없는 음.
포인트: 情=ジョウ, 景=ケイ. 장음 주의.

questions.stem: この世代の人たちはコンピューターの知識が乏しいように思う。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: とぼしい is correct.

**Question Translation**  
"この世代の人たちはコンピューターの知識が乏しいように思う。"  
→ "It seems that people of this generation have insufficient knowledge about computers."

**Explanation**  
The kanji "乏しい" is read as **とぼしい**, which means *lacking* or *insufficient*. This reading fits the context of the sentence, which talks about a lack of computer knowledge.

**Other Options**  
1. くわしい – Means *detailed* or *well-informed* (kanji: 詳しい), which is opposite in meaning and doesn't fit here.  
3. ますしい – Not a standard reading of 乏しい. Could be confused with 貧しい, meaning *poor*.  
4. あやしい – Means *suspicious* or *dubious* (kanji: 怪しい), which does not match the context.

Only **とぼしい** matches the kanji **乏しい** in this context.
questions.expl_ko:
정답: 2번 「乏(とぼ)しい」 — 부족하다, 모자라다. 「知識が乏しい」는 자주 쓰는 결합.
오답: 1 くわしい(詳しい·정통하다)는 의미는 비슷한 맥락이지만 한자가 다름. 3 ますしい·4 あやしい(怪しい·수상하다)는 한자가 다름.
포인트: 乏=ボウ/とぼ-しい.

questions.stem: ボランティアでお年寄りの介護をしている。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: かいご is correct.

**Question Translation**  
"ボランティアでお年寄りの介護をしている。"  
→ "I am providing care for the elderly as a volunteer."

**Explanation**  
The kanji "介護" is read as **かいご**, which means *nursing care* or *caregiving*. This is the correct reading based on the context of the sentence related to caring for the elderly.

**Other Options**  
1. かいごう – This is not a standard reading of 介護.  
2. かんごう – Not a valid reading or meaning of 介護.  
4. かんご – Means *nursing* in terms of a medical profession (kanji: 看護), but does not match 介護.

Only **かいご** matches the kanji **介護** in this context.
questions.expl_ko:
정답: 3번 「介護(かいご)」 — 간병, 돌봄.
오답: 1 かいごう·2 かんごう는 없는 음. 4 かんご는 「看護」(간호)와 헷갈리는 함정.
포인트: 介=カイ, 護=ゴ. 介(かい)와 看(かん)을 혼동하지 않기.

questions.stem: 今ごろになって焦ってもしかたない。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: あせっても is correct.

**Question Translation**  
"今ごろになって焦ってもしかたない。"  
→ "It’s no use getting flustered at this point."

**Explanation**  
The kanji "焦って" is read as **あせって**, which means *to be flustered* or *to panic*. This reading appropriately describes the action in the sentence.

**Other Options**  
2. しかっても – Suggests *to scold* (kanji: 叱って), and does not match 焦って.  
3. まよっても – Means *to get lost* or *to hesitate* (kanji: 迷って), which is not suitable here.  
4. いのっても – Means *to pray* (kanji: 祈って), and does not fit 焦って.

Only **あせって** matches the kanji **焦って** in this context.
questions.expl_ko:
정답: 1번 「焦(あせ)っても」 — 초조해해도, 서둘러도.
오답: 2 しかっても(叱る·꾸짖다), 3 まよっても(迷う·헤매다), 4 いのっても(祈る·기도하다)는 한자가 다름.
포인트: 焦=ショウ/あせ-る/こ-げる.

questions.stem: 高速道路の建設については、賛否が分かれた。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: さんぴ is correct.

**Question Translation**  
"高速道路の建設については、賛否が分かれた。"  
→ "Opinions were divided on the construction of the expressway."

**Explanation**  
The kanji "賛否" is read as **さんぴ**, which means *approval and disapproval* or *pros and cons*. This reading correctly reflects the concept of divided opinions in the sentence.

**Other Options**  
1. さんぷ – Not a standard reading of 賛否.  
2. さんぽ – Does not relate to 賛否; translates to *a walk* (散歩) with different kanji.  
4. さんび – Does not fit; commonly reads as *praise* (賛美) with different kanji.

Only **さんぴ** is appropriate for the kanji **賛否** in this context.
questions.expl_ko:
정답: 3번 「賛否(さんぴ)」 — 찬반, 가부.
오답: 1 さんぷ·2 さんぽ(散歩)·4 さんび는 없는 음 또는 다른 단어.
포인트: 否=ヒ. 「賛否が分かれる」(찬반이 갈리다) 빈출 결합.

questions.stem: この仕事は、山本さんにまかせておけば安心です。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: 任せて is correct.

**Question Translation**  
"この仕事は、山本さんにまかせておけば安心です。"

questions.stem: この時期に旅行するなら、かさは欠かせない。

"If you are traveling during this season, you cannot do without an umbrella."

**Explanation**  
The key word in the sentence is "欠かせない" (kakanai), meaning "indispensable" or "cannot do without." The phrase "ないと困る" (nai to komaru) accurately captures this idea, indicating that not having something (in this case, an umbrella) would cause inconvenience or problems. - The phrase "欠かせない" is often used to indicate something that is essential or cannot be overlooked, particularly in contexts where something is necessary or unavoidable.

Answer 4 is correct.

栽培（さいばい） — cultivation, growing (plants)

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
In this field, we cultivate vegetables without using pesticides.

**Explanation**  
The word **栽培** specifically refers to cultivating or growing plants or crops. The sentence "野菜を栽培しています" (cultivating vegetables) is a natural and appropriate use of the word, as it involves growing plants.

→ My parents cultivate cows at the farm to make cheese.

→ I am cultivating my six-month-old baby now.

→ I cultivated insect eggs I found in the garden and kept an observation diary.

"栽培" is not used for insects or eggs. The word "飼育" would be appropriate for breeding insects.

"栽培" should be used in the context of plants or crops, emphasizing agricultural or gardening activities. It is unsuitable for animals, humans, or non-plant-related scenarios.

questions.stem: 急激
opts: イベントの開催日が近くなり、準備が急激
新しい駅ができて、市の人口が急激
このパンは非常に人気があり、朝8時に開店すると急激

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
急激（きゅうげき） — sudden, rapid, drastic

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
A new station was built and the city's population is increasing rapidly.

**Explanation**  
The word **急激** is used to describe significant and abrupt changes or actions, typically quantifiable or measurable. "人口が急激に増加" (population is increasing rapidly) fits this meaning well, as population changes can be objectively measured and often happen noticeably with new infrastructure.

**Other Options**

① イベントの開催日が近くなり、準備が__急激__に進められている。  
→ As the event date approaches, preparations are being advanced rapidly.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
While "急激" might work, "急速に進められている" (advancing rapidly) is more natural. "急激" suggests drastic change, which isn't typically the connotation here.

③ このパンは非常に人気があり、朝8時に開店すると__急激__に売れていく。  
→ This bread is very popular, and once the store opens at 8, it sells rapidly.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
"急激" isn't the best fit here. "急に" (quickly) or "すぐに" (immediately) would be more conversational when talking about selling speed.

④ 松田選手が現れると、ファンの人たちが__急激__に取り囲んだ。  
→ When player Matsuda appeared, fans quickly gathered around him.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
While "急激" can imply speed, "一斉に" (all at once) or "急に" would capture the quick, sudden action more accurately in this context.

**Usage Note**  
"急激" is used in contexts where changes are fast, significant, and often measurable, such as "増加" (increase), "変化" (change), or in technical and broader impacts rather than common, everyday actions or subjective perceptions.

questions.stem: 漏れる
opts: ジュースを注ぎすぎて、コップから漏れて
転んでしまって、ひざから血が漏れて
水道管に穴があいているのか、水が漏れて

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
漏れる（もれる） — to leak, to escape

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
There might be a hole in the water pipe because water is leaking.

**Explanation**  
The word **漏れる** is used to describe something physically escaping or leaking out of a confined space. "水が漏れている" (water is leaking) appropriately describes the leakage from a water pipe, a common usage of this term.

**Other Options**

① ジュースを注ぎすぎて、コップから漏れてしまった。  
→ I poured too much juice, and it leaked out of the cup.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
While technically possible, "漏れる" is not typically used for overflow from a cup. More natural would be "溢れた" (overflowed), implying excess liquid spilling over.

② 転んでしまって、ひざから血が漏れてきた。  
→ I fell, and blood leaked from my knee.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
"漏れる" might seem fit for blood leaking, but it's more naturally used for inanimate substances. In medical contexts, "出る" or "流れる" is preferred for bleeding.

④ 悲しい映面を見たせいで、涙が漏れてきた。  
→ Because I saw a sad scene, tears leaked.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
Here, "漏れる" is not used to express tears. Instead, "溢れた" (overflowed) or "こぼれた" (spilled) should be used metaphorically for tears.

**Usage Note**  
"漏れる" is ideal for scenarios where liquid escapes from a contained system like pipes or sealed objects. It’s less suitable for discussing emotions or biological functions like tears or bleeding, where other verbs are more common.

questions.stem: 傾向

**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
傾向（けいこう） — tendency, trend

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
Recently, there is a tendency for family members to eat separately.

**Explanation**  
The word **傾向** refers to a general direction or trend in behavior or characteristics. "傾向がある" (there is a tendency) is a common way to express a pattern or habitual behavior that occurs often. In sentence 2, it naturally describes a common societal pattern in eating habits.

**Other Options**

① ファッション誌によると、今年は黄色が傾向するそうだ。  
→ According to fashion magazines, yellow tends to trend this year.

"傾向する" is incorrect. A better choice would be "流行する" (to trend) or "人気がある" (to be popular) to describe fashion trends.

③ 姉は日本文学の研究に傾向している。  
→ My sister is inclined towards researching Japanese literature.

"傾向している" is awkward here. Use "傾いている" or "興味がある" to describe personal inclinations or interests naturally.

→ This slope has a steep tendency, making it hard to bike.

"傾向" does not describe physical inclinations. Use words like "勾配" (gradient) or "傾斜" (slope) for describing physical steepness.

**Usage Note**  
"傾向" is typically used to discuss general patterns or trends, often in statistical, social, or habitual contexts. It is not suitable for expressing individual preferences, physical inclinations, or trends in popularity directly.

questions.stem: さっさと
opts: いつまでもテレビを見てないで、さっさと
雷が鳴り出したと思ったら、さっさと
買ってまだ一週間なのに、さっさと
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
さっさと — quickly, promptly, without delay

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
Instead of watching TV forever, quickly get your homework done.

**Explanation**  
The word **さっさと** conveys a sense of promptness or urgency in completing a task without delay. In sentence 1, telling someone to stop watching TV and start homework quickly fits the typical use of **さっさと** to describe doing tasks promptly.

**Other Options**

② 雷が鳴り出したと思ったら、__さっさと__雨が降り出した。  
→ As soon as I thought I heard thunder, the rain quickly started falling.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
"さっさと" implies human intentionality, while "早速" or does not fit the pattern of suddenly starting natural phenomena, such as rain following thunder. More suitable words include "すぐに" (immediately) or "たちまち" (in no time).

③ __さっさと__着くので、もう少しそこで待っていてください。  
→ Since I'll arrive quickly, please wait a bit longer there.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"さっさと" usually involves completing a task quickly by effort, not estimating arrival time. It's more natural to use "すぐに着く" (I'll arrive soon), which focuses on temporal proximity rather than action.

④ 買ってまだ一週間なのに、__さっさと__壊れた。  
→ Even though I bought it just a week ago, it quickly broke.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"さっさと" doesn't fit with unexpected breakdowns of objects. "すぐに壊れた" (it quickly broke) or "すでに壊れた" (it's already broken) are better and more typical usages in this context.

**Usage Note**  
"さっさと" is commonly used to order tasks or actions to be completed promptly and with human control, often in imperative forms. It typically doesn't apply to natural events or states of objects and is not used for emphasizing the speed of unexpected occurrences.

questions.stem: A「田中さんに話があるんだけど、今、会議中？」B「うん。」A「じゃあ、会議が終わるのを待つ（　　　）ないわ。」
questions.expl:

**Question Translation**

B: "Yes."  
A: "Then, I have no choice but to wait for the meeting to finish."

**Explanation**  
The correct choice here is しか because it is often paired with a negative verb to express that there is no alternative or choice other than doing something. In this context, it conveys that the speaker has no option but to wait until the meeting concludes.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 2: だけ**  
  だけ means "only" as well, but it is typically used in positive sentences to state exclusivity without the nuance of a negative necessity that しか provides. Here, the sentence structure and negative context are not suitable for だけ.
  
- **Answer 3: まで**  
  まで means "until" and is used to indicate the time or extent something continues to happen. It is not appropriate here because the structure does not grammatically fit the context of indicating limited options that しか covers.
  
- **Answer 4: さえ**  
  さえ means "even" and is used to add emphasis, often highlighting unexpected situations. It does not fit in this context where the implication focuses on the lack of alternatives.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
しか is commonly paired with a negative form of the verb to create a structure that demonstrates that there is no choice or alternative, creating a nuance that highlights limitations. This is a key grammar pattern in understanding its usage in negative contexts to express necessity or shortfall in options.

questions.stem: この道路拡張計画を（　　　）にあたっては、市民の皆様のご理解が必要です。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: 進める is correct. It means "when proceeding with" or "at the time of proceeding with."

**Question Translation**  
"When proceeding with this road expansion project, the understanding of all the citizens is necessary."

**Explanation**  
The phrase "にあたって" is used to mean "at the time of" or "when doing" something, and it requires a verb in the dictionary form (plain form) to be placed before it. Therefore, "進める" (to proceed) fits correctly in this context as it represents the plan/action of proceeding with the project.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 進めた - This is the past tense form of the verb, meaning "proceeded". "にあたって" does not pair with the past tense since it implies a future or ongoing process.
- Answer 3: 進めたい - This form means "want to proceed," which denotes desire rather than an objective action and is not compatible with the purpose of "にあたって" which is more factual and neutral.
- Answer 4: 進めよう - This is the volitional form, which is like saying "let’s proceed" or "I will proceed". It implies intention or suggestion, which does not match the requirement for a neutral description of the future events or plans.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The grammar pattern "にあたって" (ni atatte) is crucial for this question. It indicates a specific point in time related to a particular action or situation, usually involving significant preparation, consideration, or planning. It is commonly used in formal and written contexts.

questions.stem: もう酒は飲まないと ______ ★ ______  ______　絶対に守りたい。
questions.expl:
Answer (★ Position)
Answer 3: 以上は

Correct Order
1 → 3 → 2 → 4
📌 決めた → 以上は → どんなに → 誘われても

Chunk-by-Chunk Breakdown
① 決めた — “decided”; completes the clause after と (“もう酒は飲まないと決めた”).
③ 以上は — “since / now that … is the case”; attaches directly to 決めた to form 決めた以上は.
② どんなに — “no matter how …”; pairs with ～ても.
④ 誘われても — “even if (I’m) invited”; completes the concessive set phrase どんなに～ても.

Reconstructed Sentence
もう酒は飲まないと**決めた以上は、どんなに誘われても、**絶対に守りたい。
→ “Since I’ve decided not to drink anymore, I absolutely want to stick to it, no matter how much I’m invited.”

Why This Order Works
・**V-と＋決めた＋以上は** is a fixed logical pattern meaning “now that I’ve decided…”.
・**どんなに～ても** must stay together to express “no matter how… even if…”.
・This yields a natural flow: decision ⇒ logical obligation ⇒ concession.

포인트: 「〜以上は」(~한 이상은)+「どんなに〜ても」(아무리 ~해도). 결심한 이상 어떤 권유에도 흔들리지 않겠다.

③ いられなく — “cannot help but …”; continues the pattern (…いられなく～).

② 何分 — “no matter how many minutes …”; quantifier for concessive pattern.
① 待っても — “even if (I) wait”; pairs with 何分 (何分待っても).
④ 先に進まないので — “since it wouldn’t proceed”; gives the reason for the next action.

Reconstructed Sentence
パソコンの電源を入れたのだが、画面に「お待ちください」という**メッセージが出たまま、何分待っても先に進まないので、**電源を入れ直した。
→ “I turned on the computer, but the ‘Please wait’ message stayed on the screen and even after waiting many minutes it wouldn’t proceed, so I restarted it.”

Why This Order Works
・**何分＋Vても** forms “no matter how many minutes (I) …”.
・Reason clause **～ないので** naturally precedes the remedial action.

questions.stem: （電話で）A「すみません、来週の2時からの会議ですが、その時間、別の用件が入ってしまいまして、もしそちらのご都合が ______ ______ ★ ______　、いかがでしょうか。」B「こちらは大丈夫ですよ。」
opts: 変更していただけると
questions.expl:
Answer (★ Position)
Answer 2: 変更していただけると

Correct Order
4 → 3 → 2 → 1
📌 よろしければ → 4時以降に → 変更していただけると → ありがたいんですが

Chunk-by-Chunk Breakdown
④ よろしければ — “if it’s alright with you”; polite conditional to check the other party’s convenience.
③ 4時以降に — “to after four o’clock”; proposed new time.
② 変更していただけると — “if you could change it …”; polite request framing.
① ありがたいんですが — “I’d appreciate it, but …”; softens/hedges before “いかがでしょうか”。

Reconstructed Sentence
（電話で）
A: すみません、来週の2時からの会議ですが、その時間、別の用件が入ってしまいまして、もしそちらのご都合が**よろしければ、4時以降に変更していただけると、ありがたいんですが、**いかがでしょうか。
→ “I’m sorry—about the meeting from 2:00 next week, I’ve had another appointment come up. If it’s alright on your side, if you could move it to after 4 o’clock, I’d really appreciate it—would that be okay?”

Why This Order Works
・Polite request flow: **よろしければ** (condition) → propose time (**4時以降に**) → request action (**変更していただけると**) → soften with **ありがたいんですが** before asking.

questions.stem: 20年前に初めてこの歌手の歌を聞いたとき、 ______ ______ ______ ★
opts: なんと美しい声なんだろう
questions.expl:
Answer (★ Position)
Answer 2: よく覚えている

Correct Order
4 → 1 → 3 → 2
📌 なんと美しい声なんだろう → と思った → のを → よく覚えている

Chunk-by-Chunk Breakdown
④ なんと美しい声なんだろう — “What a beautiful voice!”; the quoted thought.
① と思った — “(I) thought”; closes the quote.
③ のを — nominalizes the prior clause for use with 覚えている.
② よく覚えている — “(I) remember well”.

Reconstructed Sentence
20年前に初めてこの歌手の歌を聞いたとき、**「なんと美しい声なんだろう」と思ったのを、よく覚えている。**
→ “When I first heard this singer 20 years ago, I clearly remember thinking, ‘What a beautiful voice!’”

Why This Order Works
・The memory construction is **[S と(は)思った]＋のを＋覚えている**.
・The quoted exclamation precedes **と思った**, which then is nominalized by **のを** to attach to **覚えている**.

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4: 思えなかったからだ is correct. It means "because I couldn't find it interesting."

**Question Translation**  
I had previously read some rakugo in class and didn't find it very interesting, so I thought just listening to the story would be boring, and I was also worried about whether I could understand it.

**Explanation**  
The sentence explains the writer's initial disappointment with the cultural experience of rakugo, due to a previous class reading experience where it wasn't appealing. The use of から (kara) in 思えなかったからだ conveys causality; it's an explanation of why the writer thought listening to rakugo might be boring. It effectively links the lack of interest during the previous experience with the assumption that attending a live rakugo performance might not be engaging either.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 思えなかっただ is incorrect because だ simply concludes a statement without providing a causal explanation, which is needed in this context to connect the writer's prior experience and feelings about listening to rakugo.
- Answer 2: 思えなかったほどだ suggests "to the extent that I couldn't find it interesting," which implies a degree rather than a reason, thus not fitting the context of explaining why listening might be boring.
- Answer 3: 思えなかっただけだ implies "just because I couldn't find it interesting," suggesting a limit rather than providing a cause-and-effect relationship. The context needs a reason for the writer's thought process, making から more appropriate.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The use of から (kara) is a key grammar point as it signals causation or reasoning. It is frequently used in Japanese to link cause and effect and explain the rationale for thoughts or actions, making it an essential particle to understand for expressing why something is the case.

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: ところが is correct. It means "however" or "on the contrary."

**Question Translation**  
While I was listening to rakugo, I laughed a lot. The rakugo performer's movements and the way they used their voice were really interesting, and I could understand the scenes well. They portrayed two or more roles, like a parent and child, by changing gestures and speech styles, progressing the conversation. Without standing up, they conveyed moving from a house to a store by swaying their body as if walking. The mimicked eating movements appeared as though they were genuinely eating something.

**Explanation**  
The sentence juxtaposes the speaker's initial expectation of boredom with their experience of actually enjoying and understanding the performance. ところが is used to introduce an unexpected result or contradiction to what was previously stated, making it a perfect fit here. The passage describes the speaker's skepticism about rakugo but then reveals that they found it entertaining and insightful once they began observing the performance.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: しかも means "moreover" or "furthermore." It is used to add additional but related information, which does not fit here, as the sentence is not adding related information but rather presenting a contrast.
- Answer 2: すなわち means "that is" or "in other words." It is used for rephrasing or clarifying a statement, which does not match with presenting a contrast between expectations and reality in this context.
- Answer 4: したがって means "therefore" or "consequently." It is used to indicate a causal relationship, which is not appropriate here because the sentence outlines an unexpected contrast, not a cause-effect relationship.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The term ところが is crucial for expressing contrast or exception in narratives or discussions. Understanding how to use conjunctions like ところが helps in recognizing shifts or surprises in texts, which is an important skill for reading comprehension at advanced levels of Japanese proficiency.

opts: 楽しむようにするのだ
楽しむことになったのだ
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 楽しむものなのだ is correct. It means "something to enjoy."

**Question Translation**  
Rakugo is something to be enjoyed through the simultaneous performance of the storyteller's actions and narration.

**Explanation**  
In the context of the passage, the author is explaining their changed impression of rakugo. Initially, they thought rakugo might be boring and hard to understand. However, after experiencing it, they realized that rakugo involves the storyteller's expressions and actions, making it enjoyable. The phrase 楽しむものなのだ ("something to enjoy") perfectly captures this realization, emphasizing that rakugo is inherently enjoyable due to the performer's skills.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: 楽しむはずなのだ suggests "something that should be enjoyed." This is too presumptive, implying a preconceived expectation rather than a realization after experiencing rakugo.
- Answer 3: 楽しむようにするのだ implies "to make it enjoyable," suggesting an effort or requirement which doesn’t fit the context of the author's newfound appreciation.
- Answer 4: 楽しむことになったのだ means "ended up enjoying it," which would focus too much on the outcome rather than the nature of rakugo as depicted by the author.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The term もの (mono) is used to describe the essential nature or characteristic of something, often conveying an inherent quality or truth about it. In this sentence, it suggests that rakugo's fundamental characteristic is that it is enjoyable because of the interplay of the performer's actions and storytelling. Understanding how ものなのだ emphasizes the essence of the subject is crucial in grasping the intended meaning of sentences like this.

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: どんな表現 is correct. It means "what kind of expressions."

**Question Translation**  
Do rakugo storytellers make what kind of expressions?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the curious nature and diverse expressions in rakugo performances. The word "どんな" (donna), meaning "what kind of," is used to inquire about the variety of expressions that rakugo performers use. Given the context, the author expresses curiosity about the different types of expressions rakugo storytellers might utilize throughout their performances. It fits seamlessly into the sentence by forming the question: "Do rakugo storytellers make what kind of expressions?"

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: その表現 (sono hyougen) means "that expression." Using "その" implies a specific set of expressions already mentioned, which doesn't fit the context, as the passage does not refer to specific expressions previously.  
- Answer 3: 表現 (hyougen) means "expression," but without a specific qualifier like "どんな," it doesn’t properly convey the intended inquiry into the variety of expressions used by rakugo storytellers.  
- Answer 4: こういう表現 (kou iu hyougen) means "such expressions" or "this kind of expression." It suggests a particular type or example discussed prior to this sentence, which does not suit the scenario as the variety is yet to be explored, making it inappropriate here.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The phrase "どんな表現" uses the interrogative adjective "どんな," which is used to ask about the nature or types of things. Recognizing how "どんな" frames a question can help students understand inquiries about various aspects of a topic. Similarly, understanding how rakugo performers convey nuances through expressions can expand students' grasp of both cultural and linguistic elements in Japanese.

questions.stem: ある物質の働きについて、この文章からわかることは何か。
opts: 人間の持つ嫌なにおいを防ぐ
人々の気持ちを落ち着かせる。
落ち葉や枯れ木を腐りにくくする。
木々がもともと持っているにおいを消す。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: 人々の気持ちを落ち着かせる (ひとびとのきもちをおちつかせる) is correct. It means "to calm people's feelings."

**Question Translation**  
What can be understood about the function of a certain substance from this passage?

**Explanation**  
The passage describes a substance that trees produce for protection. This substance has several effects, including preventing the growth of insects and bacteria, neutralizing unpleasant odors from decomposed leaves and wood, and calming human nerves, contributing to the sense of relaxation when one enters a forest. Therefore, the function "to calm people's feelings" accurately reflects the effect on humans described in the last part of the passage.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 人間の持つ嫌なにおいを防ぐ (にんげんのもついやなにおいをふせぐ) means "to prevent bad odors from humans." The passage does not mention preventing human odors; instead, it mentions removing unpleasant odors from natural decomposition in forests.
  
- Answer 3: 落ち葉や枯れ木を腐りにくくする (おちばやかれきがくさりにくくする) means "to make fallen leaves and dead wood less likely to rot." The passage indicates the substance eliminates bad smells resulting from rot but doesn't prevent the rotting process itself.

- Answer 4: 木々がもともと持っているにおいを消す (きぎがもともともちているにおいをけす) means "to eliminate the trees' inherent smell." The passage states that the substance contributes to the fresh smell of the forest, not that it eliminates it.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The key vocabulary in understanding this passage includes the phrase "神経を安定させる" (しんけいをあんていさせる), meaning "to stabilize the nerves." This phrase directly supports the correct answer by explaining the calming effect of the substance on humans. Recognizing compound verbs such as "安定させる" (to stabilize/calm) is crucial in comprehension.

questions.stem: このメールの用件は何か。
opts: ポスターの作り方に間違いがないか確認してほしい。

ポスターを休日に提出させてほしい。

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4: ポスターを郵送で提出させてほしい is correct. It means "to allow submitting the poster by mail."

**Question Translation**  
What is the purpose of this email?

**Explanation**  
The email is written by a representative of a painting circle who is requesting permission to submit a poster by mail. The writer mentions that they cannot bring the poster directly to the reception during the center's open hours due to work commitments and asks if they can deliver it via mail instead. Answer 4 accurately captures this request for permission to submit the poster by mail, aligning with the content of the email.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: ポスターの作り方に間違いがないか確認してほしい ("Would like to confirm if there is any mistake in the poster creation") does not fit because the email states that the poster was created according to the website instructions without issues. The sender is not requesting a confirmation or check for mistakes.
- Answer 2: ポスターの提出が遅れることを許可してほしい ("Would like permission for late submission of the poster") is incorrect as the email does not mention any request for a late submission or delay; it concerns the method of submission via mail.
- Answer 3: ポスターを休日に提出させてほしい ("Would like permission to submit the poster on a holiday") is incorrect because the email does not discuss submitting on a holiday. The sender explicitly mentions the issue is with weekday opening hours.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The phrase "郵送での提出を認めていただくことはできませんでしょうか" uses formal language and a respectful request form, indicating a polite inquiry for permission. This construction is typical in formal requests, especially in written correspondence. Recognizing polite request patterns can help understand the intent of communication in such contexts.

**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: 買いたいと思っている商品が環境に良いか悪いかを、このサイトで調べることができる is correct. It means "You can check on this site whether the product you want to buy is good or bad for the environment."

**Question Translation**  
Which describes the convenient point about this internet site?

**Explanation**  
The passage describes a website run by an environmental group where you can find information about products that are good for the environment. It provides details about a wide range of products and services, including their recycling status, ease of repair, and durability. The key convenience mentioned is the ability to compare and check the environmental friendliness of products you are considering purchasing, which aligns with Answer 2.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 1:** 買いたいと思う商品についてこのサイトを通してメーカーから直接買うことができる means "You can buy the product you want directly from the manufacturer through this site." The passage does not mention purchasing directly through the site; it focuses on providing information for comparison.
- **Answer 3:** このサイトには高齢者が使いやすいさまざまな家電製品やホテルの情報が載っている means "This site contains information on various home appliances and hotels that are easy for senior citizens to use." The passage does not mention a focus on senior accessibility.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- "環境のためによい商品" (かんきょうのためによいしょうひん) means "products that are good for the environment."
- The verb "調べる" (しらべる) means "to check" or "to investigate," highlighting the function of the site in helping users determine the environmental impact of products.

Answer 4: 事務用品の注文、管理方法の変更を知らせる is correct. It means "to inform about the change in the ordering and management method of office supplies."

**Question Translation**  
What is the main purpose of this document?

**Explanation**  
The document is about a change in the method of ordering and managing office supplies. It previously involved centralized ordering and management by the general affairs section, but starting in August, each section will order and manage supplies directly. questions.stem: 筆者は、人材が公正に評価されないと組織はどうなると述べているか。
opts: 短期間で人材を育てられなくなる。
優秀な人材を獲得できなくなる。
組織の活力を維持できなくなる。
組織への関心が薄くなる。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**
Answer 3 is correct. It means "The organization won’t be able to maintain its vitality."

**Question Translation**
"According to the author, what happens to an organization when personnel are not evaluated fairly?"

**Explanation**
The passage says that organizations or societies without fair evaluation and competition will "必ず衰退する" (will inevitably decline) over the long term. Decline means losing energy/vitality (活力). Therefore, "組織の活力を維持できなくなる" matches the author’s point.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**
1. 短期間で人材を育てられなくなる — "They won’t be able to train personnel in a short time."  
→ The text notes that育成 (training) takes time, but it does not say unfair evaluation causes an inability to train in the short term.

2. 優秀な人材を獲得できなくなる — "They won’t be able to acquire excellent personnel."  
→ The passage says organizations are eager to secure talent, but the stated consequence of unfair evaluation is long-term decline, not specifically failure to hire.

4. 組織への関心が薄くなる — "Interest in the organization will fade."  
→ This effect is not mentioned; the author focuses on systemic decline (衰退), not on members’ interest.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**
・衰退する＝to decline, deteriorate.

questions.stem: 「僕はやりたくないなあ。」とあるが、T男はなぜ「いいところ探し」をやりたくないと言ったのか。

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 自分自身の長所が見つけられないから is correct. It means "because he cannot find any good points about himself."

**Question Translation**  
The question asks, "T男 said, 'I don't want to do it,' but why did T男 say he didn't want to do the 'finding good points' exercise?"

**Explanation**  
The correct answer is best supported by T男's words in the passage: "だって、どうせ僕にはいいところなんてないもん" (because I don’t have any good points anyway). This statement directly reflects a lack of self-esteem and belief that he has no positive qualities, aligning perfectly with the answer choice indicating he can't find his own good points.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: 自分の良さを書くのがはずかしいから (because it’s embarrassing to write about his own good points): The passage doesn’t suggest T男 is embarrassed to write about his qualities; it highlights his belief that he has none.
- Answer 3: 友達の長所を見つけるのは難しいから (because finding his friends' good points is difficult): The resistance in T男’s comment is personal, about his self-view, not about the challenge of evaluating others.
- Answer 4: 友達のことがまだよくわからないから (because he doesn’t know his friends well yet): This option doesn't relate to T男's comment that focuses on his self-perceived lack of good traits.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- いいところ探し: This phrase means "finding good points," which in the context suggests identifying and appreciating positive traits in oneself and others. Understanding this exercise is key to realizing T男's lack of self-esteem.
- つぶやく (whisper/utter): Provides insight into T男’s internal struggle as he's quietly expressing his self-doubts.

クラス全員の名前のある紙に、長所がある友達について書いて、先生に提出する。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: クラス全員の名前のある紙に、一人ひとりの長所を書いて、先生に提出する is correct. This means "On the paper with the names of all the class members, write each person's strengths and submit it to the teacher."

**Question Translation**  
How is "looking for good points" conducted?

**Explanation**  
The passage describes an activity where students are asked to identify and write down positive traits for each of their classmates. The teacher distributes a sheet with everyone’s names, and each student needs to identify and write down a positive trait (長所, ちょうしょ) for each classmate. Answer 3 accurately captures this task: listing the strengths of each classmate on a sheet containing all their names, which will be submitted to the teacher.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 先生からもらった紙に、いいところのある友達の名前を書いて提出する translates to "Write the names of friends with good points on the paper received from the teacher and submit it." This is incorrect because students are supposed to write down the strengths of every classmate, not just selectively name friends with positive traits.
- Answer 2: 先生からもらった紙に、クラス全員の名前といいところを書いて提出する translates to "On the paper received from the teacher, write the names and good points of all class members and submit it." Although similar in meaning, the distinction lies in the process: students focus on writing the positive traits, which is a more detailed action than simply listing classmate names along with traits.
- Answer 4: クラス全員の名前のある紙に、長所がある友達について書いて、先生に提出する translates to "Write about friends with strengths on the paper with all class member names and submit it to the teacher." Incorrectly suggests the focus on only some friends with notable strengths, not all classmates.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- The term 長所 (ちょうしょ), meaning "strengths" or "good points," is essential here, emphasizing the positive traits being listed for each individual.
- The structure focuses on detail and specificity in the task, reflecting an understanding of recognizing strengths (長所を見つける目を持ってほしい), crucial for interpersonal development among students. This aligns with the teacher's goal to foster positive engagement and self-esteem within the class.

**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: クラスのみんなが互いにほかの友達のことを知り、いいところを認め合うようにすること is correct. It means "To encourage everyone in the class to get to know each other and recognize each other's good points."

**Question Translation**  
What is the purpose of "looking for good points"?

**Explanation**  
The passage describes an activity organized by a teacher to help students get to know each other better. The teacher's intent is to create deeper relationships among students by having them identify and appreciate each other's strengths. This intention is clearly stated when the teacher expresses a desire for the students to have the ability to discover the good aspects of their classmates ("友達のことを知ってほしい、長所を見つける目を持ってほしい"). Furthermore, the activity involved writing down positive traits about each classmate, supporting the goal of mutual acknowledgment and understanding. Therefore, Answer 2 accurately captures this intention by emphasizing the mutual recognition of one another's good points.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: This option focuses on T男's adaptation to the new class. Although it touches on an aspect of the situation (T男 gaining confidence), the primary purpose of the activity was class-wide interaction and mutual recognition, not specifically about T男's adaptation.
- Answer 3: This option implies that the focus is on finding unnoticed strengths and discussing them publicly. However, the passage does not indicate a requirement to present these findings to the class; it primarily discusses individual reflection and acknowledgment.
- Answer 4: This option suggests that the activity is intended to help students realize their own shortcomings by looking for others' strengths. The passage's emphasis, however, is on recognizing others' positive attributes rather than self-reflection on one's own deficiencies.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- **長所** (ちょうしょ): A key vocabulary word meaning "strong points" or "good traits." Understanding this term is essential as it is central to the purpose of the exercise described in the passage.
- **馴染む** (なじむ): Meaning "to fit in" or "to get used to," important for understanding why Answer 1 is primarily focused on T男 and might not address the overall purpose.
- The narrative demonstrates the cultural and educational goal of fostering a positive and collaborative classroom environment by recognizing and appreciating diversity in personal strengths. This is a common theme in Japanese classroom activities focused on group cohesion.

questions.stem: 筆者は、人々がなぜ「職業声」を使うと思っているか。

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 自分が仕事をするうえで求められていると思っているから is correct. It means "because they think it is required for them to do the job."

**Question Translation**  
What does the author think about why people use 'professional voices'?

**Explanation**  
In the passage, the author discusses the concept of '職業声' or 'professional voice' and suggests that people believe they must adopt such a voice to perform their jobs. The passage explicitly mentions that individuals think they have to become a certain type of person as indicated by their choice of voice in specific jobs, treating it like a manual or uniform. Thus, the correct answer is that people perceive it as a requirement for their job performance.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: 自分が仕事に慣れていると思われたいから (because they want to be seen as familiar with the job) is incorrect. The passage does not suggest that people use professional voices to appear accustomed to their jobs; rather, it discusses perceived necessity rather than familiarity.
- Answer 3: 自分がその仕事に合わないと思われたくないから (because they do not want to be seen as unsuited to the job) is incorrect. The focus in the text is on conforming to expectations, not avoiding negative judgments about one's fit.
- Answer 4: 自分の中で仕事のイメージを明確にできると思っているから (because they think they can clarify the job image for themselves) is incorrect. The passage mentions external expression and conformity to expectations rather than internal clarity or image determination.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The term '職業声' (しょくぎょうごえ) refers to an artificial voice that people use in professional settings, akin to wearing a uniform. The passage emphasizes societal and role expectations, suggesting that adopting such a voice is perceived as required, thus masking one's individuality for professional conformity. Understanding such contextual applications of vocabulary can be crucial for comprehension questions on the JLPT.

**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 残された時間ですべてを利用することができないから is correct. It means "Because I cannot use all of these things in the time I have left."

**Question Translation**  
Question: ① "この物最はムダだなぁ" (This stuff is wasteful) is mentioned here, but why does the author think so?

The passage discusses how the author realized the sheer quantity of unused items while moving houses. The realization of their limited remaining life leads to viewing these possessions as wasteful. - Answer 2: 使っていない道具も一緒に運ばなければならないから (Because I have to transport unused tools as well.)

- Answer 4: 使わなくなったものがたくさんあるから (Because there are many items I no longer use.)

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The expression "この物最はムダだなぁ" uses "ムダ" (muda), meaning wasteful, which reflects not just on unused items but a deeper reflection on the futility of ownership given one's finite lifespan. The passage discusses the concept of "預かりものの思想" ("the philosophy of entrusted items"). This philosophy suggests that all things we own, like land, houses, or tools, are merely borrowed from the world during our lifetime. We cannot take them with us after death, implying that our ownership is temporary and not absolute. Answer 2 directly captures this philosophical viewpoint, emphasizing the impermanence and the temporary nature of ownership as the central idea.

預かりもの (あずかりもの) combines "預かる" meaning "to look after or hold temporarily," and "もの" meaning "thing," referring to the notion of temporary stewardship over items. This idea is key to understanding the impermanent ownership being conveyed in the passage.

Passage B, a high school student's opinion, acknowledges the library's policy and reasoning. However, the student feels that libraries should serve as study spaces for students, particularly those preparing for exams, indicating an understanding but not complete agreement. This reflects Answer 2 accurately, as the student understands A's request but argues for an alternative approach that would allow study in the library.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: The passage in A does not express a desire for an increase in users like B, who wish to use the library as a study space. In fact, A explicitly requests against such use.
- Answer 3: A's notice focuses on the act of using library spaces for personal study being an issue, not on students talking or making noise as the primary problem.
- Answer 4: B does not suggest that the library should provide exam preparation books. Instead, B focuses on the need for the library to serve as a study space.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- The phrase "お願い" (onegai) in the context of A's notice is a polite way to ask users to refrain from certain behaviors. It's crucial to the understanding of A's polite yet firm request to align the use of library spaces with their intended purpose. 
- The term "納得" (nattoku) can be translated as "agreement" or "consent," and its use in Answer 2 indicates partially understanding the reasoning but without full acceptance.

questions.stem: 筆者によると、人間の「オフライン状態」とはどういう状態か。
opts: 他人と交流したいと思わない。
コンピュータをあまり使わない。
新しいことをすることは少ない。
日常生活の中でしか新しいことを探さない。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: 新しいことをすることは少ない is correct. It means “There are few new activities.”

**Question Translation**  
According to the author, what is the “offline state” for humans?

**Explanation**  
In the passage, a human's "offline state" is described as similar to daily life, where there isn't much absorption of new information or activities. The passage contrasts this state with the "online state," where new information is integrated, possibly leading to changes in behavior and thoughts. Answer 3 is correct because it aligns with the description that, in the offline state, new activities are few and existing information or routines are primarily used.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 他人と交流したいと思わない means "not wanting to interact with others." This is not mentioned in the context of the offline state. The focus is not on people interaction, but rather on the integration of new information.
- Answer 2: コンピュータをあまり使わない means "not using computers much." Although the metaphors of offline and online are used with computers, this statement doesn’t directly describe the human offline state depicted in the passage.
- Answer 4: 日常生活の中でしか新しいことを探さない means "only seeking new things in daily life." This is incorrect because the passage states that little new is incorporated in daily offline life, not about where newness is sought.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The passage uses the contrast between "オフライン状態" (offline state) and "オンライン状態" (online state) metaphorically to explain human behavior. Recognizing this metaphorical use is crucial to understanding the thematic comprehension of the passage. The term 日常生活 (にちじょうせいかつ) "daily life," suggests routine and regularity in activities.

questions.stem: 筆者によると、人間は旅に出るとどうなるか。
opts: 自分とは違うやり方があることに気づく。
自分とは違うことをしている人を批判する。
自分のやり方が自分に合っているとわかる。
毎日の生活で感じた疑問を解決できる。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 自分とは違うやり方があることに気づく。 This means "To realize that there are ways different from one's own."

**Question Translation**  
According to the author, what happens to humans when they go on a journey?

**Explanation**  
The passage explains that when humans travel, they naturally switch to an "online state" where they are more open to new information, much like a computer connected to a network. While traveling, people encounter different environments and customs, which leads them to question the routines they have always accepted as the norm. As a result, they become aware of alternative methods and ways of living different from their usual habits, aligning with the idea of realizing there are other approaches ("自分とは違うやり方があることに気づく").

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: 自分とは違うことをしている人を批判する ("Criticize people doing things differently") does not fit because the text argues against this viewpoint, suggesting an open-minded approach to understanding other cultures rather than being judgmental.
- Answer 3: 自分のやり方が自分に合っているとわかる ("Understand that one's own way suits oneself") contradicts the main point of the passage, which is about opening up to different perspectives and questioning one's habits rather than reinforcing existing beliefs.
- Answer 4: 毎日の生活で感じた疑問を解決できる ("Be able to resolve doubts felt in daily life") is not specific to the journey’s experience described, and the passage mentions that travel incites questioning rather than immediate resolution of daily life's doubts.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- **オフライン/オンライン状態**: These terms are used metaphorically to describe a person's openness to new ideas.
- **灯台下暗し**: This proverb indicates that the familiar environment makes it difficult to gain new insights, thus justifying the need for travel to gain different perspectives.

questions.stem: 旅について、筆者の考えに合うのはどれか。
opts: 自分の知識を広げるために、旅をするといい。
忙しい日常生活を忘れるために、旅は必要だ。
旅によって、自分の人生を見つめ直すことができる。
旅をたくさんすれば、自分の人生を変えることができる。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: 旅によって、自分の人生を見つめ直すことができる。 It means "Through traveling, one can reconsider or reevaluate their life."

**Question Translation**  
Which option aligns with the author's thoughts on traveling?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses how traveling puts a person in an "online state," allowing them to encounter new information and experiences. This exposure to unfamiliar environments challenges habitual behaviors and encourages introspection about one's life and actions. The author emphasizes that travel provides an opportunity to see things from a new perspective, separate from one's everyday routine, making it a fit for "reconsidering one's life" through reflection prompted by new and diverse experiences.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 自分の知識を広げるために、旅をするといい。 This means "It's good to travel in order to broaden your knowledge." The passage suggests gaining new insights but focuses more on reconsidering one's own life rather than solely expanding knowledge.
- Answer 2: 忙しい日常生活を忘れるために、旅は必要だ。 This means "Travel is necessary to forget the busy everyday life." While the passage mentions stepping away from day-to-day routine, it doesn't primarily advocate travel as an escape from busyness.
- Answer 4: 旅をたくさんすれば、自分の人生を変えることができる。 This means "If one travels a lot, they can change their life." The passage indicates introspection and reconsideration, not directly asserting that frequent travel leads to life changes by itself.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- オンライン状態 (オンラインじょうたい): "Online state," implies being open to new information and adaptability.
- オフライン状態 (オフラインじょうたい): "Offline state," refers to operating on existing knowledge without new inputs.
- 見つめ直す (みつめなおす): To reconsider or reevaluate, particularly in the context of self-reflection and life choices.  
Understanding these terms is crucial, as they inform the passage's theme of how travel affects one's approach to learning and introspection.

**Question Translation**

**Explanation**
Rules: Only members (一般会員／シニア会員) can use the service; delivery area is limited; max 3 boxes; general members need a total of ≥3,000円; senior members can use 1 box per 1,000円 (typo in notice intended as 1,000円). opts: 常温の商品で、午前10時から午後4時までに済ませる。
常温の商品で、正午から午後10時までに済ませる。
常温の商品と冷凍の商品で、午前10時から午後4時までに済ませる。

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**
Answer 2 is correct. It means "Only room-temperature items can be sent, and the acceptance must be completed between noon and 10 p.m." 

**Question Translation**
"Mr./Ms. Kayama is a general member and can use this delivery service. Today, they plan to buy room-temperature items and frozen foods. They want delivery tomorrow morning. What can be sent, and by what time window must they finish the acceptance?"

**Explanation**
・冷蔵・冷凍は対象外 → Only 常温 (room-temperature) items are deliverable.  
・To receive **tomorrow morning (翌日の午前9時～正午)**, acceptance must be either **正午～午後4時 (choose B)** or **午後4時～午後10時 (choose A)**. Combining these gives **正午～午後10時**. Therefore option 2 matches both the allowable goods and the correct acceptance window.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**
1. 常温の商品で、午前10時から午後4時までに済ませる — "Room-temperature items, finish acceptance between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m."  
→ 10:00～正午の受付 gives **same-day** delivery, not tomorrow morning. Also it omits the valid 4:00–10:00 p.m. window.

3. 常温の商品と冷凍の商品で、午前10時から午後4時までに済ませる — "Room-temperature **and** frozen items; finish 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m."  
→ 冷凍は対象外, and the time window has the same problem as (1).

4. 常温の商品と冷凍の商品で、正午から午後10時までに済ませる — "Room-temperature **and** frozen items; finish noon–10:00 p.m."  
→ 冷凍は対象外 (cannot be sent), so incorrect even though the time window itself would work.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**
・対象外＝not covered/eligible.  
・配達受付＝delivery acceptance (sign-up) time; 配達時間＝actual delivery window.  
・［A］/［B］ are selectable time slots; choose the one matching the desired delivery.

questions.script_html: 問題5 問題5では長めの話を聞きますメモを取っても構いません 1番問題用紙に何も印刷されていません まず話を聞いてくださいそれから質問と選択肢を聞いて 1から4の中から最も良いものを一つ選んでください では始めます市の図書館で館長と職員2人が図書館のサービスについて話しています 最近図書館の利用者数が伸び悩んでいるので市民にもっと利用してもらえるよう何かできることはないか考えてみたいと思います 今ポイントカードを発行して貸し出し数に応じてポイントを付けてますよねポイントが溜まったら文房具を挙げてるんですけどあまり喜ばれていないように思うんです 品物を変えてみてはどうでしょうかそうですね 他に何か案はありますかあとはもっと楽しく本を借りてもらえるように2、3冊袋に入れて貸し出すのはどうですか 本のタイトルを秘密にしてどういうことですか?恋愛とか冒険とか テーマに沿って本を集めて数冊袋に入れておくんですどんな本が入っているか袋を開けるまでわからないようにして なるほどでもそれだと読んだことがある本が入っているってこともありますよね その時は交換できるようにしたらいいですよあのまずは今やっている館内の見学会をホームページとかでもっと宣伝するのはどうですか?これまでもホームページやチラシで十分宣伝してきてますからね それなら親子で参加できるイベントを増やしたらどうですか今定期的にやってる工作や折り紙の教室いつも人気で定員いっぱいですよね そうするとイベント当日は職員の数を増やす必要が出てくるし準備の負担も増えますね ポイントカードの制度は経費がかかるからこの際やめてもいいかなって思ってるんです今回は手間も経費も少なくて済みそうなさっきのユニークな案 試してみましょう図書館の利用者を増やすために何をすることにしましたか? 1 ポイントと交換する品物を変える2 テーマごとに本を袋に入れて貸し出す3 見学会の宣伝に力を入れる4 親子で参加できるイベントを増やすまず話を聞いてください それから2つの質問を聞いてそれぞれ問題用紙の1から4の中から 最も良いものを一つ選んでくださいでは始めます 市民運動公園で係の人がイベントの説明をしています本日の防災フェアは4つの会場に分かれています 第一会場の体育館では災害時怪我をした際の応急手当を実際に体験できます第二会場の運動場ではヘリコプターの離陸訓練をご覧いただけます 先着10名の方は実際にヘリコプターに乗ることもできますただし18歳以上の方に限ります それから第三会場の駐車場では消防車を展示しており運転席に座ってみることができます 第4会場のプールでは午後1時より服を着たまま泳ぐ訓練をご覧いただけます各会場での体験や見学を通して防災について学んでいただきたいと思います へー色々あるんだねーヘリコプターなんてなかなか乗れないから乗ってみたいな 行ってみない私は高いところ苦手だから下で見てるね えーじゃあ消防車にしようかせっかくの頃乗りたいのに乗ったら先着順どころ急いで行こう わかった他にどこか行きたいところある 服を着たまま泳ぐっていうのを興味あるけどあと3時間もあるから応急手当はどう役立ちそうだしそうだねじゃあ次はそれに行こう 質問12人はまずどこへ行きますか質問に2人は次にどこへ行きますか

questions.script_html: 問題5 問題5では長めの話を聞きますメモを取っても構いません 1番問題用紙に何も印刷されていません まず話を聞いてくださいそれから質問と選択肢を聞いて 1から4の中から最も良いものを一つ選んでください では始めます市の図書館で館長と職員2人が図書館のサービスについて話しています 最近図書館の利用者数が伸び悩んでいるので市民にもっと利用してもらえるよう何かできることはないか考えてみたいと思います 今ポイントカードを発行して貸し出し数に応じてポイントを付けてますよねポイントが溜まったら文房具を挙げてるんですけどあまり喜ばれていないように思うんです 品物を変えてみてはどうでしょうかそうですね 他に何か案はありますかあとはもっと楽しく本を借りてもらえるように2、3冊袋に入れて貸し出すのはどうですか 本のタイトルを秘密にしてどういうことですか?恋愛とか冒険とか テーマに沿って本を集めて数冊袋に入れておくんですどんな本が入っているか袋を開けるまでわからないようにして なるほどでもそれだと読んだことがある本が入っているってこともありますよね その時は交換できるようにしたらいいですよあのまずは今やっている館内の見学会をホームページとかでもっと宣伝するのはどうですか?これまでもホームページやチラシで十分宣伝してきてますからね それなら親子で参加できるイベントを増やしたらどうですか今定期的にやってる工作や折り紙の教室いつも人気で定員いっぱいですよね そうするとイベント当日は職員の数を増やす必要が出てくるし準備の負担も増えますね ポイントカードの制度は経費がかかるからこの際やめてもいいかなって思ってるんです今回は手間も経費も少なくて済みそうなさっきのユニークな案 試してみましょう図書館の利用者を増やすために何をすることにしましたか? 1 ポイントと交換する品物を変える2 テーマごとに本を袋に入れて貸し出す3 見学会の宣伝に力を入れる4 親子で参加できるイベントを増やすまず話を聞いてください それから2つの質問を聞いてそれぞれ問題用紙の1から4の中から 最も良いものを一つ選んでくださいでは始めます 市民運動公園で係の人がイベントの説明をしています本日の防災フェアは4つの会場に分かれています 第一会場の体育館では災害時怪我をした際の応急手当を実際に体験できます第二会場の運動場ではヘリコプターの離陸訓練をご覧いただけます 先着10名の方は実際にヘリコプターに乗ることもできますただし18歳以上の方に限ります それから第三会場の駐車場では消防車を展示しており運転席に座ってみることができます 第4会場のプールでは午後1時より服を着たまま泳ぐ訓練をご覧いただけます各会場での体験や見学を通して防災について学んでいただきたいと思います へー色々あるんだねーヘリコプターなんてなかなか乗れないから乗ってみたいな 行ってみない私は高いところ苦手だから下で見てるね えーじゃあ消防車にしようかせっかくの頃乗りたいのに乗ったら先着順どころ急いで行こう わかった他にどこか行きたいところある 服を着たまま泳ぐっていうのを興味あるけどあと3時間もあるから応急手当はどう役立ちそうだしそうだねじゃあ次はそれに行こう 質問12人はまずどこへ行きますか質問に2人は次にどこへ行きますか
